findings.text: You must have a design system codebase and a Figma design library.
findings.quote: To use this guide, you need a design system codebase that contains components, and a Figma design library (a Figma file that contains your root design system components).

findings.text: You must install Node.js 18 or newer.
findings.quote: Install Node.js 18 or newer

findings.text: You must generate a personal access token with specific scopes.
findings.quote: Generate a personal access token with the Code Connect scope set to Write and the File content scope set to Read.

findings.text: You must have a Dev or Full seat on a Professional, Organization, or Enterprise plan.
findings.quote: A Dev or Full seat on the Professional, Organization, or Enterprise plan.

findings.text: Figma recommends using template files for connecting design components to code.
findings.quote: In this guide, we’ll get you set up with Code Connect CLI using template files — the recommended approach for connecting your design components to code.

findings.text: Install the Code Connect command line tool.
findings.quote: Install the Code Connect command line tool

findings.text: Create a figma.config.json file in the root of your project.
findings.quote: Create a figma.config.json file in the root of your project:

findings.text: Create a .figma.ts file for your component.
findings.quote: Create a .figma.ts file for your component.

findings.text: Publish the files using the command line tool.
findings.quote: npx figma connect publish --token=PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN

findings.text: Figma recommends using granular scopes instead of the deprecated files:read scope.
findings.quote: While this scope will continue to work, it's highly recommended you use the granular scopes Figma provides. Because files:read is extremely permissive, more limited scopes such as file_content:read and file_comments:read provide enhanced security and stability

findings.text: You must register your app in the My apps section of your Figma account if you are building an app for others to use.
findings.quote: If you plan on building a fully-fledged app, that others can share and use, then you can register your app by heading to My apps in your Figma account.

findings.text: The first step to using the API is to sign up and create a Figma account.
findings.quote: If you’re not already using Figma, the first step is to sign up and create an account.

findings.text: After creating an account, you must authenticate using either OAuth2 or access tokens.
findings.quote: Once you have a Figma account, the next step is to authenticate with the API. This can be done using either OAuth2 or access tokens.

findings.text: Figma recommends creating an OAuth app to use OAuth 2 for making requests on behalf of users.
findings.quote: Recommended: Create an OAuth app to use OAuth 2, which lets you make requests with access tokens that you obtain on behalf of the users of your app.

findings.text: OAuth apps allow acting on behalf of individual users, while plan access tokens are for organization-level automation.
findings.quote: Use an OAuth app if your application needs to act on behalf of individual Figma users, and for the Embed API. Use a plan access token for organization-level automation like CI/CD pipelines, logging, and other tasks that shouldn't be tied to a specific user.

findings.text: An OAuth app must be associated with a team or organization.
findings.quote: The OAuth app must be associated with a team or organization.

findings.text: Authentication codes expire 30 seconds after being issued.
findings.quote: Authentication codes expire 30 seconds after being issued. You must exchange the code for an access token by calling https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token within 30 seconds of the user completing the OAuth grant.

findings.text: Access tokens expire after 90 days by default.
findings.quote: By default, access tokens expire after 90 days.

findings.text: WebView access to the Figma OAuth flow is not supported.
findings.quote: Important: Regardless of how you provide the URL itself, the user must access the authentication URL using a web browser, not an embedded WebView inside your application. WebView access to the Figma OAuth flow is not supported.

findings.text: Navigate to the apps page to create a new app.
findings.quote: Click My Apps in the top toolbar, or go to figma.com/developers/apps. In the upper-right corner of the page, click Create a new app.

findings.text: Enter a name and select a team or organization for the app.
findings.quote: Enter a name for your OAuth app, and select a team or organization. The OAuth app must be associated with a team or organization.

findings.text: Click Create to finish the initial app creation.
findings.quote: Click Create.

findings.text: Securely store the Client ID and Client Secret.
findings.quote: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret for your OAuth app and store them securely. This is the only opportunity you have to obtain the Client Secret.

findings.text: Add one or more redirect URLs on the OAuth credentials page.
findings.quote: On the OAuth credentials page, click Add a redirect URL and add one or more redirect URLs for your OAuth app.

findings.text: Select the required scopes on the OAuth scopes page.
findings.quote: On the OAuth scopes page, select one or more scopes that you want to use for your OAuth app.

findings.text: Publish the app on the Publish page.
findings.quote: On the Publish page, select whether you want your app to be public or private.

findings.text: Navigate to the apps page to start the creation process.
findings.quote: Click My Apps in the top toolbar, or go to figma.com/developers/apps.

findings.text: Initiate the creation of a new OAuth app.
findings.quote: In the upper-right corner of the page, click Create a new app.

findings.text: Provide a name and associate the app with a team or organization.
findings.quote: Enter a name for your OAuth app, and select a team or organization. The OAuth app must be associated with a team or organization.

findings.text: Finalize the initial creation of the app.
findings.quote: Click Create.

findings.text: Securely store the provided Client ID and Client Secret.
findings.quote: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret for your OAuth app and store them securely. This is the only opportunity you have to obtain the Client Secret.

findings.text: Complete the initial creation process.
findings.quote: Click Done.

findings.text: Authentication code expiry time.
findings.quote: Authentication codes expire 30 seconds after being issued. You must exchange the code for an access token by calling https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token within 30 seconds of the user completing the OAuth grant.

findings.text: Default access token expiration.
findings.quote: By default, access tokens expire after 90 days.

findings.text: WebView access is not supported for the OAuth flow.
findings.quote: Important: Regardless of how you provide the URL itself, the user must access the authentication URL using a web browser, not an embedded WebView inside your application. WebView access to the Figma OAuth flow is not supported.

findings.text: To publish an OAuth app to the Figma Community, it must be a public app.
findings.quote: To publish your OAuth app to the Figma Community, it must be a public app. You can start with an existing public OAuth app or use a draft OAuth app. For a draft OAuth app, you'll need to make it public during the configuration flow.

findings.text: Navigate to the OAuth apps list at figma.com/developers/apps and select the app to publish.
findings.quote: In the list of your OAuth apps at figma.com/developers/apps, click the OAuth app that you want to publish to the Figma Community.

findings.text: Click Publish on the left side of the configuration modal.
findings.quote: On the left side of the configuration modal, click Publish.

findings.text: Select Public if publishing a draft app and check the box to list the app on the community.
findings.quote: If you're publishing a draft OAuth app, select Public. Select List this app on community.

findings.text: Provide the author, tagline, description, landing page URL, support contact, and tags on the listing setup page.
findings.quote: Select the author that will appear for your app. You can select either yourself, or the team or organization your OAuth app is assigned to. Enter a tagline. Enter a description of your app. Enter a landing page URL for your app. Enter a support contact.

findings.text: Upload a cover image on the images page.
findings.quote: Set a cover image for your app.

findings.text: Provide a justification for each selected OAuth scope.
findings.quote: For each scope, describe why your app needs access to that scope.

findings.text: Enter testing instructions for the app reviewer.
findings.quote: Enter all the steps that are required for in order for Figma's OAuth app reviewer to successfully test your application and understand its features.

findings.text: Certify the submission and click Submit for review.
findings.quote: When you’re ready, click the I certify… checkbox, and then Submit for review.

findings.text: Navigate to the OAuth apps list at figma.com/developers/apps and select the app to publish.
findings.quote: In the list of your OAuth apps at figma.com/developers/apps, click the OAuth app that you want to publish to the Figma Community.

findings.text: Click Publish on the left side of the configuration modal.
findings.quote: On the left side of the configuration modal, click Publish.

findings.text: Select Public and List this app on community, then click Next.
findings.quote: If you're publishing a draft OAuth app, select Public. Select List this app on community. Click Next.

findings.text: Fill in the community listing details including author, tagline, description, landing page, support contact, and tags.
findings.quote: Enter a tagline. Enter a description of your app. You can use markdown in the description, and text formatting controls are provided. Enter a landing page URL for your app. Enter a support contact. Select relevant tags for your app.

findings.text: Upload a cover image and optional carousel images.
findings.quote: Set a cover image for your app. Optionally, add up to nine images of your app to the carousel for your app's Community page.

findings.text: Provide justification for each requested OAuth scope.
findings.quote: For each scope, describe why your app needs access to that scope.

findings.text: Provide testing instructions and credentials for the reviewer.
findings.quote: Enter all the steps that are required for in order for Figma's OAuth app reviewer to successfully test your application and understand its features. If necessary for working with your application, provide a free trial URL or login credentials that the OAuth app reviewer can use to access your application.

findings.text: The app must be a public app to be published to the Figma Community.
findings.quote: To publish your OAuth app to the Figma Community, it must be a public app.

findings.text: A logo is required for the community listing.
findings.quote: When you publish an app to the Figma Community, you'll need to provide several things: A logo

findings.text: A tagline of 100 characters or less is required.
findings.quote: A tagline (100 characters or less)

findings.text: A landing page URL is required.
findings.quote: A landing page URL

findings.text: A support contact (email or URL) is required.
findings.quote: A support contact (email or URL)

findings.text: Apps must go through a review process before they can be used outside the team or organization where they were registered.
findings.quote: Before a Figma Community App may be used outside of the team or org where it was registered, it needs to go through our review process.

findings.text: You must register a separate app for each application that calls Figma's APIs.
findings.quote: You’ll need to register a separate Figma Community App for each application that’s calling Figma’s APIs.

findings.text: Apps that read or modify a Figma file without user awareness and consent may be rejected.
findings.quote: In connection with this, we may reject Figma Community Apps that read or modify a Figma file without a user’s explicit awareness and consent

findings.text: Apps cannot require users to install separate packages that manipulate Figma on the Web or the Desktop App.
findings.quote: Figma Community Apps can only leverage official APIs provided by Figma and cannot require users to install separate packages that manipulate Figma on the Web or the Desktop App.

findings.text: Attempts to exploit the API will result in immediate denial of API access.
findings.quote: Any attempts to exploit the API (deceitful manipulation of user files, theft of data) will result in immediate denial of API access.

findings.text: Apps are not permitted to index file content available in a customer's account.
findings.quote: Figma does not currently permit Figma Community Apps to index file content available in a Figma customer's account.

findings.text: Apps are not permitted to perform bulk export of Figma file content.
findings.quote: Figma does not currently permit bulk export of Figma file content by Figma Community Apps.

findings.text: You must choose whether your OAuth app is private or public.
findings.quote: Decide whether you want your app to be private or public. Private apps are limited to your organization and don't require Figma approval. Public apps can be used by anyone with a Figma account and must be reviewed and approved by Figma.

findings.text: Public apps require Figma approval.
findings.quote: Public apps can be used by anyone with a Figma account and must be reviewed and approved by Figma.

findings.text: Figma recommends using template files for connecting design components to code.
findings.quote: In this guide, we’ll get you set up with Code Connect CLI using template files — the recommended approach for connecting your design components to code.

findings.text: You can write template files using an AI coding agent that supports the Figma MCP server.
findings.quote: If you’re using an agent that supports the Figma MCP server, the figma-code-connect skill writes template files for you.

findings.text: You can write template files manually by creating .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
